configurePresets.name: default
configurePresets.description: The default backend. src/ with NEVPT2_GPU_BACKEND=CUDA: nvcc -> a host binary with every kernel linked in (rdm_launch/kernels.cu, rdm_accumulate, f3_digest, f3_scatter, device_einsum) on WarpWraps' wwr* runtime names.

nevpt2.//: NOT a cacheVariables entry, and that is the point: `cacheVariables` is a free-form map where EVERY key becomes a -D, so a `//`-prefixed note in there is not a comment -- it is a cache variable literally named `//CUDAToolkit_ROOT`, and CMake reports it on every single configure as `Manually-specified variables were not used by the project`. A spurious warning on every configure is one people stop reading. `vendor` is the spec's own escape hatch: CMake checks that it is a map and otherwise ignores it.
nevpt2.CUDAToolkit_ROOT: PINNED ON PURPOSE. This box carries six CUDA installs (12.1, 12.9, 13.0, plus the cuda/cuda-12/cuda-13 symlinks) and find_package(CUDAToolkit) picked 12.9 on its own -- which has no CUBLAS_COMPUTE_64F_EMULATED_FIXEDPOINT, so the --cublas digest failed to compile while everything else succeeded. /usr/local/cuda is the conventional 'current' symlink and is 13.0 here and in docker/Dockerfile.cuda. Override with -DCUDAToolkit_ROOT=... for a different toolkit.

configurePresets.name: workstation
configurePresets.description: The SAME configuration as `default` into a different build dir, so a host build and a container build can coexist without reconfiguring each other -- a CMake cache records absolute paths, and the two mount the workspace at different ones.

configurePresets.name: hip
configurePresets.description: The same src/ tree with NEVPT2_GPU_BACKEND=HIP: -x hip -> a host binary with every kernel linked in (rdm_launch/kernels.cu, rdm_accumulate, f3_digest, f3_scatter, device_einsum) on wwr* names. No --cublas. Needs no CUDA toolkit.

configurePresets.name: asan
configurePresets.description: Sanitizer tier: Debug + AddressSanitizer on host code -- CXX units and the host side of every .cu (nvcc's host compiler becomes the same clang) -- with device code uninstrumented. Its test preset sets ASAN_OPTIONS=protect_shadow_gap=0, which the CUDA runtime needs under ASan. Separate build-asan/ dir.

configurePresets.name: ubsan
configurePresets.description: Sanitizer tier: Debug + UBSan with -fno-sanitize-recover on host code (CXX and the host side of every .cu), so the first finding aborts the test. Device code uninstrumented. Separate build-ubsan/ dir.

configurePresets.name: compute-sanitizer
configurePresets.description: Sanitizer tier: a Debug CUDA build (device code with -lineinfo) whose demo ctest entries each run under NVIDIA compute-sanitizer. NEVPT2_COMPUTE_SANITIZER_TOOL picks the tool (memcheck by default; initcheck, racecheck, synccheck): reconfigure with -D to switch, no rebuild needed. Its test preset runs only the `small` CAS(4,4)/CAS(8,8) entries and the canaries. CUDA only -- a HIP configure refuses the option.

configurePresets.name: hip-asan
configurePresets.description: The asan preset against ROCm/HIP: Debug + AddressSanitizer on host code (CXX units and the host side of every -x hip .cu); -fno-gpu-sanitize keeps device code uninstrumented (device ASan needs an xnack+ target; gfx1200 has no xnack). Separate build-hip-asan/ dir.

configurePresets.name: hip-ubsan
configurePresets.description: The ubsan preset against ROCm/HIP: Debug + UBSan (-fno-sanitize-recover) on host code, device code uninstrumented. Separate build-hip-ubsan/ dir.

configurePresets.name: coverage
configurePresets.description: Release (what `fast` tests) + clang source-based coverage (-fprofile-instr-generate -fcoverage-mapping) on host CXX units; device libraries (every .cu) stay uninstrumented. Its test preset writes one .profraw per process into build-coverage/profraw/; devtools/coverage.sh configures, builds, tests and turns them into a report. Release, not Debug: source-based counters are inserted before the optimizer, so the counts are exact at -O3, and a Debug HIP build compiles device code -O0 too (the --ozaki entry alone then runs for many minutes). Separate build-coverage/ dir.

configurePresets.name: hip-coverage
configurePresets.description: The coverage preset against ROCm/HIP: the same host CXX units instrumented, every -x hip .cu left alone. Separate build-hip-coverage/ dir.

configurePresets.name: compile-cuda
configurePresets.description: Compile-and-link only: NEVPT2_BUILD_TESTING=OFF, so no ctest entry is registered. There is NO CI in this project (see docs/testing.md, 'No CI, and the local gate') This is the configuration for checking that the tree still builds without running anything, e.g. on a box with no card.

configurePresets.name: compile-hip
configurePresets.description: The same shape as compile-cuda for the other backend, and what devtools/cross-backend-check.sh drives (CROSS_CHECK_PRESET). Compiling is the point: src/ is one tree built for both backends, so a CUDA-only spelling outside src/cublas/cublas_emul.cpp (CUDA-only by design) breaks only the HIP side and nothing else catches it. --device-only builds just the nevpt2_device_libraries umbrella.

testPresets.name: default
testPresets.description: Everything: the golden entries (labelled `gpu`, each needs a real card) and the GoogleTest unit tier (labelled `unit`). Only the host-only unit suites run card-free -- `ctest -LE gpu` selects them, and they prove logic, never an energy.

testPresets.name: unit
testPresets.description: The GoogleTest unit tier only (test/, label `unit`): one entry per suite plus each binary's <target>.SuiteListIsComplete drift guard. The suites not also labelled `gpu` need no card.

testPresets.name: fast
testPresets.description: CAS(10,10) (~2s/run) and the small CAS(4,4)/CAS(8,8) cases; drops the ~47s CAS(12,12) case.

testPresets.name: hip
testPresets.description: The ROCm runtime tier. Needs /dev/kfd + /dev/dri and the render/video groups -- see devtools/config.sh, ROCM_GROUPS.

testPresets.name: sanitizer
testPresets.description: Every sanitizer test preset runs the `small` CAS(4,4)/CAS(8,8) entries, the GoogleTest unit tier (`unit`) and the canaries its build registered, nothing else (docs/testing.md, 'Sanitizers').

testPresets.name: asan
testPresets.description: The small cases + the ASan canary. protect_shadow_gap=0: the CUDA runtime's address reservations collide with ASan's shadow gap otherwise. LSan suppressions: cmake/nevpt2_lsan.supp (vendor runtimes only).

testPresets.name: ubsan
testPresets.description: The small cases + the UBSan canary.

testPresets.name: compute-sanitizer
testPresets.description: The small cases, the unit tier and the configured tool's canaries; the entries that touch the GPU run under compute-sanitizer. Drops the `death` suites: EXPECT_DEATH forks, and compute-sanitizer does not follow a forked child.

testPresets.name: hip-asan
testPresets.description: The asan test preset on ROCm/HIP. The LSan suppressions matter here: the ROCm runtime leaks ~6 KB of its own at exit.

testPresets.name: hip-ubsan
testPresets.description: The ubsan test preset on ROCm/HIP.

testPresets.name: coverage
testPresets.description: What `fast` runs (every entry not `slow`: the golden cases and the unit tier), each process writing build-coverage/profraw/<pid>.profraw. %p, not a merge pool: one file per process is what makes a parallel ctest -j safe. devtools/coverage.sh empties the directory before and merges it after.

testPresets.name: hip-coverage
testPresets.description: The coverage test preset on ROCm/HIP.
